{{Quote|If we can get the Ansionians to commit to pulling out of the Republic, no one will really care. But because of their alliances, their withdrawal should be enough to sway their already vacillating partners in both the Malarian Alliance and the Keitumite Treaty to follow.|Presidente Shu Mai|<ref name="Approaching" />}}
The '''Dbari system''' was a [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Star system/Legends|star system]] that was home to the [[Dbarian]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], it was affiliated via the [[Malarian Alliance]] to three other [[Star/Legends|star]] systems. That alliance was part of a larger network of forty systems linked by various alliances and treaties to each other, centered on the inconspicuous [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ansion/Legends|Ansion]].

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], when members of the Malarian Alliance were considering seceding from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of the Independent Systems]] sought to facilitate the secession of the entire network of systems affiliated with Ansion. The Separatist plans were foiled by a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Border dispute on Ansion/Legends|mission to Ansion]], which resulted in the planet and its partner systems remaining loyal to the Republic.

==Description==
The Dbari system was a part of the [[Churnis sector/Legends|Churnis sector]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="EAOC" />

==History==
{{Quote|The Malarian Alliance. On the face of it, one of hundreds of such casual alliances. Keitumite Mutual Military Treaty. Never invoked, but still in force. Now, observe this.|Presidente Shu Mai, before displaying the network of star systems politically connected to Ansion|<ref name="Approaching" />}}
[[File:Ansion-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Confederacy of Independent Systems intended to use the connections of the planet Ansion to the Dbari system and others for political gain.]]
By [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="22 BBY">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[The Approaching Storm]]'', during which the [[Malarian Alliance]] is in effect, to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref> the Dbari [[Star system/Legends|system]] was a member of both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Malarian Alliance]], the latter of which placed it in a web of mutual affiliations with three other systems: the [[Mamendin system/Legends|Mamendin system]] of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] and the Mid Rim's [[Ansion system/Legends|Ansion]] and [[Malari system/Legends|Malari systems]]. In addition, Dbari, its partner systems, and the [[Keitumite Mutual Military Treaty]]&mdash;also affiliated with the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ansion/Legends|Ansion]]&mdash;all had treaties of their own with other worlds, which led to the seemingly insignificant Ansion lying at the center of a network of approximately forty [[Politics/Legends|politically]] connected [[Star/Legends|star]] systems. During the ongoing [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]],<ref name="TEA" /> signatory systems of both the Malarian Alliance and the Keitumite Mutual Military Treaty were individually considering leaving the Republic.<ref name="Approaching" />

The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] intended to facilitate the secession of Ansion from the Republic, which was predicted by the Separatists to cause a cascade of secession by all the systems linked to the planet via its treaties, as well.<ref name="TEA" /> [[Presidente/Legends|Presidente]]<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|shumai|Mai, Shu}}</ref> [[Shu Mai/Legends|Shu Mai]] of the [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]] explained the Separatist plan to the [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] industrialist [[Tam Uliss]] and his [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Unidentified Twi'lek (Tam Uliss)|companion]] during a meeting with Ansion's [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Mousul]] in a private chamber on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="Approaching" /> a Core Worlds planet serving as the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of the Republic,<ref name="TEA" /> in 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].<ref name="22 BBY" /> Mai also singled out the member systems of the Malarian Alliance,<ref name="Approaching" /> including Dbari,<ref name="TEA" /> for the group in a [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] projection of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Approaching" />

However, a [[Border dispute on Ansion/Legends|mission to Ansion]] undertaken at the [[Time/Legends|time]] by members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] on behalf of the Republic resulted in that world<ref name="TEA" /> and its partners remaining loyal to the [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] government,<ref name="Approaching" /> foiling the Separatist plans. At some point following the [[Declaration of a New Order|establishment]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the newly appointed Imperial [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] of the Churnis [[Sector/Legends|sector]] declared all existing treaties and alliances involving Ansion to be null and void.<ref name="TEA" />

==Inhabitants==
The Dbari system was home to<ref name="Planetnamia" /> the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Dbarian]] [[Species/Legends|species]].<ref name="Approaching" />

==Behind the scenes==
''[[The Approaching Storm]]'', a [[2002]] novel by [[Alan Dean Foster]], featured a holographic representation of the several unnamed star systems connected to the planet Ansion via the Malarian Alliance.<ref name="Approaching" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], subsequently identified one of those systems as the Dbari system and placed it in grid square I-6.<ref name="TEA" />
